note: BLM Eagle Lake Field Office campground on 480-acre Dodge Reservoir, an irrigation reservoir and trout fishery in remote high desert about 17 miles NE of Ravendale; a small loop of sites with picnic tables and fire rings on a juniper flat beside an open point. The ranch that holds the water rights keeps no minimum pool, so the water can drop well back by late summer; the BLM suggests calling the field office about water conditions. Access is 11 miles of unimproved dirt County Rd 506, which the BLM says is passable pulling a trailer but rough and dusty and can be impassable in wet weather. --Claude
summary: Dodge Reservoir (BLM Eagle Lake FO): BLM page + rec.gov search + Esri + 3DEP. Free (donations) confirmed; first-come confirmed (rec.gov 14887 information-only), 14-night limit added; vault toilet added, no potable water confirmed. Lakefront -> lakeview lead (loop road between every visible site and the water). Pin ~330 m off on a hillside. Phone and website correct.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (downgrade, lakefront -> lakeview): the camping is one small loop at ~40.9737,-120.1327. Its north road runs 15-20 m from the imagery water's edge (DEM 1753.8 m at the road, 1749.6 m 22 m north, 1745 m 40 m north - an easy gentle slope), and its west road is ~35-40 m from the water across an open sandy point; every spur I can see is inside the loop, so the loop road lies between the sites and the water (curation doc: a campground's own loop road means *view at best). Open ground with the water unscreened gives a lakeview floor. No site can be named on the water side of the road. The reservoir has 'no minimum pool requirement', so late-season water can be far below the imagery's edge; the imagery itself shows a little exposed shore on the north arm (near but below full). The old evidence ('a shore-access 2-track along the waterline with open primitive camping above it') describes the shore track, not identified sites. Proposed evidence: 'Esri 2026-11-26 at 40.9733,-120.1340: one loop of spurs on a juniper flat; loop road 15-40 m from the high-water edge across open ground, no spur outside it; 3DEP road 1754 m vs water edge ~1745-1749 m -> open view, loop road between -> lakeview. --Claude'
